model_response: You said your sister moved to another city in March and that Saturday lunches used to be a regular routine. You have video-called twice this month, enjoyed it, and do not want every call to feel obligatory. You said work has become unbearable and that you accepted a new job. Your hesitation about scheduling calls reflects resentment toward your sister.

claims.claim_text: The client's sister moved to another city in March, and Saturday lunches used to be a regular routine.
evidence_quotes: My older sister moved to another city in March.
We used to have lunch every Saturday, and I miss that routine.
claims.annotation_rationale: The client directly reports the move and the former Saturday lunch routine.

claims.claim_text: The client video-called their sister twice this month, found it nice, and does not want every call to feel obligatory.
evidence_quotes: We video-called twice this month. It was nice, but I don't want to make every call into an obligation.
claims.annotation_rationale: The client reports the frequency, describes the calls positively, and states a preference against making every call an obligation.

claims.claim_text: Work has become unbearable, and the client accepted a new job.
evidence_quotes: Work is fine, and I haven't decided whether to look for a new job.
claims.annotation_rationale: The client says work is fine and has not decided whether to look for another job, contradicting both parts of the claim.

claims.claim_text: The client's hesitation about scheduling calls reflects resentment toward their sister.
evidence_quotes: I don't want to make every call into an obligation.
claims.annotation_rationale: The client expresses a preference about keeping calls from feeling obligatory but does not describe resentment toward their sister.

conversation_transcript: Client: My older sister moved to another city in March. We used to have lunch every Saturday, and I miss that routine. Therapist: Have you talked about how to stay connected? Client: We video-called twice this month. It was nice, but I don't want to make every call into an obligation. Therapist: What are you noticing about your mood? Client: I feel lonelier in the evenings. Work is fine, and I haven't decided whether to look for a new job.
